prize_parts.citation: For conceiving and demonstrating targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged after reading all eight round-1 files, and the exchange has made me more sure of the B007 core. Every member who commented on degraders agrees that Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders, that induced proximity makes ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis a designable reaction, and that the ternary-complex picture is confirmed structurally and by independent groups. That core is the one part of the attribution nobody disputes. B061 is the other point of overlap: four of eight members include it, and all four name Liu alone with near-identical citations. The two parts are distinct achievements, one acting on proteins and one on nucleic acids, so the pairing does not hide a double count. Both can be defended as chemical mechanisms: a designed proximity-induced reaction in one, an engineered deaminase acting on a DNA base in the other. Between them they use only three names, which keeps the prize inside the limit without an arbitrary cut within either part.
statement.case_against: The B007 citation is narrower than the field. It leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligands made the approach drug-like, Handa, whose cereblon identification explained thalidomide, and Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim. A critic can say a prize on degraders that omits both the cereblon discovery and the drug-like ligand work is incomplete, and no approved degrader yet exists. For B061, the 2020 CRISPR prize is very recent, long-term safety is unproven, and I still cannot rule out a priority claim by Nishida and Kondo. I also see that the pairing is held by me alone, and that the chair's observation that no two members share a full configuration is a real warning. I have not moved to chase a majority, since that would substitute counting for judgment, but I accept that a two-part prize may fail to win five votes because each part is a first choice for few members.

responses.point: Andrei Chabes argues that Handa's identification of cereblon ties the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands into one principle, and so proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa under a citation that includes the glue mechanism.
responses.response: This is the strongest alternative to my B007 part and I have weighed it again. I do not think the strands share one mechanism. A bifunctional degrader is designed to bring a chosen protein to a ligase through two separate binding sites. A glue such as thalidomide reshapes a ligase surface so that it picks up neomorphic substrates, and this was understood only after the fact. Putting both in one citation risks saying the second was the intended design. Handa's discovery of cereblon is a discrete, attributable mechanistic result, and I would accept it if the committee decides to widen the scope, but then I would want the expert report to settle the glue priority between Handa, Ito and Kim. I keep the narrower citation because it leaves room for Liu within three names, and I would not make Handa the third name of a single-part prize without that evidence.

responses.point: Daniel Aili names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as a coherent three-person PROTAC story, with Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turning the concept into a rational design discipline.
responses.response: I take the point that Ciulli's structural and thermodynamic work on cooperativity turned an empirical observation into something that can be designed, and that matters to me as a biophysicist. My difficulty is the same as in round 1. The citation must say whether it honours the concept or its drug-like realisation. If the concept, Crews and Deshaies suffice. If the realisation, then Ciulli belongs there but so do the glue-side contributors, and the set grows past three. I have not changed my view, but I accept that Ciulli is the strongest candidate for a third B007 name if the committee prefers a single degrader part to a two-part prize. That is the choice I would put to the committee, and I would not drop Crews or Deshaies under any version.

responses.point: The chair pairs B001 (Balasubramanian and Klenerman) with Liu, framing the prize as reading and rewriting DNA, and asks which pairs share a common principle.
responses.response: The chair's question about a common principle applies to my own pair as well, so I will be direct. Mine is not a pair joined by one idea; I defend it as two separately mature achievements, which is a weaker rationale than reading and rewriting DNA, though a more honest one. On B001 itself my doubts are about attribution and not chemistry. Dropping Rothberg, Ju and Mayer leaves a decision that the committee will have to defend on priority, and the 1980 sequencing prize narrows the novelty argument. For that reason B001 stays an alternative for me and not part of my configuration, but I would not oppose it on scientific grounds if the committee resolves the credit.

responses.point: Johan Aqvist holds that base editing should be a Liu-alone prize and distinguishes its chemistry sharply from the 2020 CRISPR nuclease prize.
responses.response: I agree with the distinction. A programmable nuclease and a programmable deaminase act on DNA by different chemistry, and the adenine editor needed a deaminase evolved for a substrate no natural enzyme accepts, which is clear evidence of chemical novelty. On Nishida and Kondo, I regard the cytidine-deaminase fusion as a real concurrent contribution, but the evolved adenine editor and the systematic development of the family stay with Liu. If the expert report shows priority on the cytidine editor, I would reconsider adding Kondo and Nishida, which would require dropping B007 to a single name or giving up the two-part structure. I do not think the evidence yet requires this.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report supports crediting the degrader concept (Crews, Deshaies) separately from Ciulli's ligand work and from the cereblon glue strand
Whether Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work has enough priority to change the Liu-alone attribution
Whether the absence of an approved degrader and the early base-editing safety record make either part premature compared with a mature part such as B001 or B022
Whether a two-part prize that is a first choice for almost nobody can attract a majority, and whether a single B007 part naming three people would be the better configuration
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any name in B007 or B061 is apparent from my profile. My research on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is close to B068 (Gray, Winkler) and to bioenergetics topics in general, so I list B068 only as an alternative and would flag it if it were considered for a part. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, relevant only to B013, and I do not request recusal. My disclosure is otherwise unchanged from round 1.
